Pharmaceutical monitoring of a patient with elevated level of blood glucose induced by paxlovid-tacrolimus drug interactions Zhou Wei，Jiang Junjie，Wang Facai（\* Department of Pharmacy，the Lu'an Hospital Affiliated to Anhui Medical University，Lu'an 237005，China） \*Corresponding author［Abstract］ A kidney transplant patient was complicated with COVID-19. Because of the long-term use of immuno-rejection drugs，such as tacrolimus and prednisone acetate，the patient's immunity was reduced. The patient's condition worsened drastically after admission. He was treated with antiviral therapy of nematrevir tablets and ritonavir tablets. However，due to the strong drug interaction between paxlovid and tacrolimus，the blood concentration of tacrolimus in the patient increased to 43. 6 ng/ml；meanwhile，the toxic symptoms，such as nausea and vomiting，occured， and the level of fasting blood glucose was 16. 7 mmol/L. Clinical pharmacists suggested discontinuing tacrolimus immediately and monitoring blood drug concentrations daily. Resumption should be made 3 days after the end of the paxlovid treatment course and after checking blood drug concentrations. Afterwards，the blood trough concentration of tacrolimus was stabilized gradually，blood sugar returned to normal，and the patient's nausea and vomiting was gradually improved.
